dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I've heard that Cecilias only grow in remote spots at high-altitude, and that you're unlikely to ever see one unless you go looking for it.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Though they can be preserved for a long time as specimens, I can't take back the beauty they possess in the wild. It's a shame.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Shall I ask Sucrose to develop a Cecilia variant with improved soil adaptability for you?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I should warn you, though, it may very well end up with a name like "Tetratanic Ananemo Cecilia," or perhaps "Epsilon-Series Cecilia, Variation 601, Sumeru Growth-Type."

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Is this you attempting to tell a joke?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Unfortunately not. I'm being completely serious.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: In that case, I look forward to... well, whichever of those two it ends up being.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Back to our previous topic — if you wish to use antitoxic compounds from Calla Lilies in an antidote, then I have a few suggestions...
